one_liner: Go Ed25519/X25519/sr25519 library ported from curve25519-dalek; ~1.9x faster signing, ~1.7x faster verification than Go 1.17 crypto/ed25519.
what_it_does: It is a pure-Go (plus amd64 assembly) Curve25519 toolkit, mostly derived from Rust's curve25519-dalek. primitives/ed25519 mirrors crypto/ed25519 (Sign, Verify, NewKeyFromSeed, GenerateKey, crypto.Signer) and adds Ed25519ph/ctx, VerifyWithOptions with compatibility presets, a BatchVerifier and precomputed ExpandedPublicKey. primitives/x25519 mirrors x/crypto/curve25519 (X25519, ScalarBaseMult, ScalarMult). There are also sr25519, Merlin, ECVRF and hash-to-curve packages, plus a mid-level curve API whose stability is explicitly not guaranteed.
how_it_is_fast: On amd64 it runs dalek's AVX2 backend, rewritten as avo-generated Go assembly: four field elements in radix 2^25.5 are packed into YMM registers so Edwards point additions and doublings proceed four lanes at a time, and scalar field multiplication uses assembly taken from George Tankersley's ristretto255. Signing, keygen and X25519 ScalarBaseMult use a precomputed Edwards basepoint table (then convert to Montgomery form) instead of a Montgomery ladder. Single cofactored verification uses ABGLSV-Pornin multiplication, where 2-D lattice reduction shortens the scalars so fewer doublings are needed. Batch verification uses Straus's method for small batches and Pippenger multiscalar multiplication above an internal threshold, and can cache per-key NAF tables through ExpandedPublicKey.
when_to_use: Go services whose throughput is bound by Ed25519 verification, such as consensus, gossip or transparency logs on AVX2 amd64: 75 us versus 125 us per verify in the author's Go 1.17 run.

Verifying hundreds to thousands of mostly valid signatures at once, where you need cofactored or ZIP-215 semantics: 1,024 signatures took 31.7 ms versus 61.8 ms with ed25519consensus, and 24.0 ms when the keys were pre-expanded.

Workloads that repeatedly verify against the same public keys, such as validator sets. An ExpandedPublicKey costs about 11.3 us and 1.5 KB to build and saves about 9 us per verify, so it pays for itself from the second verification.
Generating many X25519 key pairs (fixed-base ScalarBaseMult): 24 us versus 107 us with x/crypto on the benchmark machine.
Code that needs explicit, selectable Ed25519 acceptance rules (stdlib-compatible, FIPS 186-5/RFC 8032, ZIP-215) or sr25519/Merlin/ECVRF in Go without cgo.
when_not_to_use: X25519 Diffie-Hellman with arbitrary peer points (variable-base ScalarMult): 106 us versus 107 us with x/crypto, so there is no gain, and Cloudflare CIRCL (BMI2) was faster at 65 us.
You need signatures accepted exactly as crypto/ed25519 accepts them, and in batches: the default semantics differ from stdlib, and the stdlib-compatible preset cannot be batch-verified.

You need numbers for current Go: every figure is from Go 1.17 on one 2021 laptop CPU. The baselines have since changed (x/crypto/curve25519 is now a thin wrapper over crypto/ecdh), and the repo publishes no newer comparison.
Secret-key hygiene or constant-time guarantees on every target: the README says it makes no attempt at memory sanitisation, and warns that wasm gives no constant-time assurances.

Toolchains or platforms off the supported list: gccgo is rejected, Go 1.18+ is enforced, CI runs only Go 1.18 on amd64 (arm64 CI is open issue #66), and no external audit is documented (issue #3 was closed without a linked report).

integration.min_toolchain: Go 1.18+ with the gc compiler (enforced by a compile-time gate in internal/toolchain; go.mod still says go 1.17); the README says it tracks the latest two Go releases
integration.platforms: 64-bit backend: amd64 (AVX2 assembly when available), arm64, ppc64, ppc64le, s390x; 32-bit backend: 386, arm, mips, mipsle, mips64, mips64le, riscv64, loong64, wasm; everything else unsupported
integration.thread_safety: not documented; Sign/Verify are stateless functions over byte slices, while BatchVerifier holds mutable state and documents no locking
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — primitives/ed25519 and primitives/x25519 copy the crypto/ed25519 and x/crypto/curve25519 function shapes, but default Verify semantics differ from stdlib (pass VerifyOptionsStdLib via VerifyWithOptions for identical acceptance), and batch verification has no stdlib equivalent

gotchas: Default Verify is cofactored, rejects small-order and non-canonical A, rejects non-canonical R and requires S < L. Mixing it with crypto/ed25519 in a consensus system can split acceptance, so pin a preset explicitly.

BatchVerifier.Verify is only faster than serial verification when every signature is valid. One bad signature triggers per-entry re-verification, and VerifyBatchOnly just returns false without saying which entry failed.
A batch containing any entry with CofactorlessVerify (for example the StdLib preset) always returns false from VerifyBatchOnly, and AddWithOptions panics on nil options.
The deprecated ScalarMult writes all zeroes for low-order points; use X25519, which returns an error. Sign allocates (64 B, 1 alloc per call) where stdlib allocates nothing.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it when you are in Go and want cgo-free Ed25519/X25519 with batch verification and configurable acceptance rules. ENG25519 (AVX-512 IFMA) and the SUPERCOP amd64-64-24k Ed25519 code are C/assembly aimed at raw cycles, and watsign targets JavaScript/wasm.
verified_claims_summary: The author's in-repo go test benchmarks (Go 1.17, Intel i7-10510U at 1.80 GHz, turbo off, AVX2 assembly on) show Ed25519 Verify at 75 us versus 125 us for crypto/ed25519 (~1.67x) and Sign at 27.5 versus 52.7 us (~1.92x). X25519 ScalarBaseMult was 24 us versus 107 us for x/crypto (~4.5x), while ScalarMult was unchanged. Batch verification of 1,024 signatures was measured against ed25519consensus, not stdlib: 31.7 ms versus 61.8 ms (~1.95x). With assembly disabled (purego), Verify was 121 us versus stdlib's 181 us.
status_note: Slow but maintained: the last commit is 2025-11-14 (String methods on key types), preceded by feature work in 2022-2023. It is BSD-3-Clause, used by oasis-core, and has 89 known importers of primitives/ed25519 on pkg.go.dev.
